[1/3] Plan lattice v0.3.0: (1) zero-dependency web server and human-friendly research studio UI in lattice/web.py with unit tests, (2) CLI web subcommand, (3) ADR-006, README and codebase map sync.

impact_assessment.why: User requested a web-based, human-easy UI for interacting with the research knowledge graph, literature discovery, claim extraction, and scientific synthesis.
impact_assessment.benefits: Humans get an intuitive visual studio with one-click demo corpus seeding, literature discovery, quote-backed claim extraction, consensus-scored synthesis, and interactive SVG subgraph visualization without external dependencies.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: REST JSON endpoints must align with repository and synthesis DTOs; dependency: zero external CDN/font URLs in HTML/CSS/JS (hygiene gate); concurrency: SQLite connection handling per HTTP request; state: idempotent demo seeding.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure dispatch_web_request function for sub-millisecond unit tests; request-scoped SQLite connection in HTTP handler; 100% self-contained HTML/CSS/JS/SVG with zero external URLs.

impact_assessment.why: Continue improving Lattice for automated literature search, knowledge creation, knowledge interaction, scientific synthesis, and human-easy web UI.
impact_assessment.benefits: Adds biomedical/open-access discovery (OpenAlex, EuropePMC) and federated search, automated claim contradiction detection and Paper x Question evidence matrices, and browser-based BibTeX/RIS/Markdown ingestion.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: existing CLI, MCP and Web API routes must remain backward-compatible; dependency: stdlib-only constraint; concurrency: multi-provider discovery timeouts; state: idempotent contradiction edge creation.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Injectable HTTP fetchers with 10s timeouts, pure analysis functions over Repository, idempotent edge insertion, and sub-millisecond unit tests per milestone.

[1/5] Data layer: add paper tags and study_type (schema v2 with v1 migration), deterministic study-type inference, and literature search matching tags, words and sentences, with failing-first tests; [2/5] propagate fields through ingest, discovery and manual paper add; [3/5] Web Studio literature search panel (tag chips, word/sentence search, study-type filter) and study-type labels on paper graph nodes; [4/5] README, ADR and knowledge-map refresh; [5/5] Phase 4 gates and delivery

impact_assessment.why: User asked for search by tags, words or sentences in the literature area and for study type to appear on graph points, so literature discovery/curation must expose searchable metadata and graph nodes must carry study-type context.
impact_assessment.benefits: Researchers can find papers in the literature list by keyword phrase, exact sentence, generated/user tags and study type; graph nodes identify the kind of study behind each paper; AI agents receive the same metadata through the shared repository.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: paper payloads gain two fields, existing v1 databases must migrate without data loss, CLI/MCP/web payloads stay backward-compatible; dependency: standard library only, no new packages; concurrency: schema migration runs once under SQLite's existing connection/busy timeout, no background writers; state: tags/study_type persist in SQLite and JSONL snapshots, inference is deterministic and leaves explicit values untouched.
impact_assessment.mitigation: add columns through an idempotent v1->v2 migration with a backup-free ADD COLUMN path, keep defaults empty so old snapshots import, cover migration and search in unit tests, and run the full project gates before committing.
